description:
FOUND s493 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the SCALING battery: 40 everyday operations, each run at N and 4N inside one process, flagged when 4N costs more than 8x (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s493/angles/scaling/scaling.pl; perl: NO operation flagged, whole battery 9.8 s; PCL at QUARTER scale: scaling.pcl.log).  37 of the 40 scale linearly under PCL (hash insert/delete/each, join, split, m//g scalar loop (#477 holds), \G lexer, s///g, substr walk, index walk, tr, sort, map/grep, sprintf, HoA, AoH, sub + method calls, file read/write/slurp).  The three that do not:

    my $s = ""; $s .= "ab" for 1 .. $n;            n=100k  4.81 s   400k 125.6 s   x26    (perl 400k: 0.02 s)
    my @a = (1..$n); $x = shift @a while @a;        n=50k   8.01 s   200k 188.9 s   x24    (perl 200k: 0.01 s)
    unshift @a, $_ for 1 .. $n;                     n=12.5k 0.51 s   50k    8.1 s   x16

`shift @a` in a loop is THE queue / worklist / argument-processing idiom and `.=` in a loop is how every report is built; a 200k-line input turns a 0.1 s perl script into minutes.  Which SHAPES of `.=` and shift are affected is measured in ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s493/probes/append-shapes.pl -> depth-append.log (append the table here when filing the fix batch: the `str-buffer` Kind-A pass covers SOME `.=` loops -- the closure / statement-modifier shape above is evidently outside it; shift is O(n) per call = the vector is copied down; perl keeps an offset).
Fix shapes (perf agent, measure first): shift = a start OFFSET in the array representation (or fill-pointer + displaced index) so shift is O(1) amortized, unshift symmetric (perl over-allocates at the front); `.=` = adjustable string with fill pointer + geometric growth on the GENERAL path, not only in the licensed pass.  Bar: the scaling battery itself (no flagged row), bench suite no slower, sweep (cl/ change).
THE INSTRUMENT (keep it): scaling.pl costs 10 s under perl and is the only test in the project that looks at the SHAPE of the cost curve; #477 (quadratic m//g) was found by accident, these three in its first run.

=== THE SHAPES TABLE (probes/append-shapes.pl under pcl, N = 50k then 200k, CPU seconds; perl: every row < 0.1 s) ===
$s .= "ab" for 1..N  (in anon sub)             1.16s   30.40s x26.2
for my $i (1..N) { $s .= "ab" }                0.00s    0.01s x0.0
my $n = $_[0]; for (1..$n) {$s .= "ab"}        0.00s    0.01s x0.0
while ($i++ < N) { $s .= "ab" }                1.21s   28.26s x23.4
$s .= "$i," (interpolated)                     0.01s    0.04s x0.0
$s = $s . "ab"                                 1.11s   24.06s x21.7
$h{k} .= "ab" (hash element)                   1.08s   24.34s x22.6
our $g .= "ab" (package var)                   1.10s   23.89s x21.8
shift @a while @a                             10.45s  165.65s x15.8
while (defined(my $x = shift @a)) {}          10.83s  179.65s x16.6
queue: push 1, shift 1 (steady size)           0.05s    0.19s x3.7
unshift @a, $_                                11.35s  187.04s x16.5
splice(@a, 0, 1) drain                        16.11s  171.47s x10.6

READ: `.=` is linear ONLY where the `str-buffer` Kind-A pass licenses it (a `for my $i (LIST) { $s .= ... }` BLOCK on a lexical).  The GENERAL path is quadratic: the statement-modifier form `$s .= "ab" for 1..N`, a `while` loop, `$s = $s . "ab"`, a HASH ELEMENT target, a PACKAGE variable -- 200k appends = 24-30 s each.  So the fix belongs in the runtime representation (p-.= on the general path appends in place: adjustable string + fill pointer, geometric growth), not in widening the pass.  `shift` costs O(length) per call: a drain of 50k = 10 s, 200k = 166-180 s, in both spellings; a steady-size queue (push 1 / shift 1 at length 100) is fine, which is why no benchmark saw it.  `unshift` and `splice(@a, 0, 1)` are the same curve.


=== USER RULING s494 (2026-09-21) ===
SCHEDULED as the NEXT PERF SLOT, ahead of #1890/#1891 (AskUserQuestion: "#2098 as next PERF slot" selected).  Launches when one of the two in-flight slots (s492b, s492c) frees; Fable writes the brief (profile FIRST: which representation makes `.=`, `shift`, `unshift` quadratic -- the three may be one cause or three).

=== s494 PROBE (Fable, 2026-09-21): the `shift` MECHANISM measured in bare SBCL 2.6.0 -- ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/p2098/disp2.lisp ===
A PCL array is an adjustable fill-pointer vector = an SBCL array HEADER over a simple data vector, and `p-shift` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) copies every element down through the generic `aref`.  Three bodies, draining N elements one shift at a time:
    today`s copy-down loop        50k  7.036 s                 (= the 8-10 s PCL measures: the loop IS the whole cost)
    (replace arr arr :start2 1)    50k  0.532 s   200k  8.997 s (13x faster, portable CL, STILL QUADRATIC)
    advance the header`s WINDOW    50k  0.001 s   200k  0.003 s (O(1) per shift)
The window = (sb-kernel:set-array-header arr data (1- avail) (1- fill) (1+ displacement) (1- dim) T nil) after clearing the vacated data slot.  CHECKED on the shifted array: aref, (setf aref), length, subseq, coerce, vector-pop, vector-push-extend, replace, adjust-array all correct; the array keeps its IDENTITY (eq); GROWTH (vector-push-extend past capacity, adjust-array) allocates fresh data and RESETS the displacement to 0 (front slots reclaimed); a DRAINED array keeps its offset (displacement 48, avail 16 after drain + one push) -- reset the window when the array becomes empty.
WHY IT IS SAFE AGAINST THE EXISTING FAST PATHS: the only two sites in the runtime that reach an array`s data vector are `%p-str-data` (strings) and `%p-vec-data`, and `%p-vec-data` answers NIL for a header with displaced-p set -- its own block comment: "NIL means not that shape (... a displaced array ...) and the caller must use its ordinary path -- the answer is identical either way".  So displaced-p MUST be T in the window call: with it NIL, `%p-vec-data`s 21 callers would index the data vector from the wrong origin = SILENT WRONG.  The cost of being safe: a shifted array takes the ordinary paths until its window resets.
NOT a function: (setf sb-kernel:%array-dimension) is not fbound in 2.6.0 (first probe attempt died "undefined function"); `set-array-header` is the one call that sets all five fields.  It is SBCL-INTERNAL => the brief requires a LOAD-TIME SELF-TEST with a loud fallback to the `replace` arm (install matrix = different SBCL versions; floor 2.5.2).
THE CALLING PATH: `my $x = shift;` in a raw-params sub binds WITHOUT p-shift; a general sub emits (p-shift @_) -- so fib/subret/methret/moo-objs are the CONTROL set of the round (a header call may cost more than copying two elements: a length threshold is decided by the number).
`.=` GENERAL PATH, read not measured: `p-.=` = (concatenate (quote string) (to-string cur) (to-string value)) -- a fresh string per append, O(length); the runtime`s law is that strings are SHARED values and nothing mutates a string it did not make (note above *p-small-fixnum-strings*), so an in-place general append needs an OWNERSHIP invariant (snapshot at every retaining store).  Brief: half one = the S1 license stops depending on the loop`s spelling (if member 1 shows the decline is not a safety condition); half two = a CENSUS of retaining sites, nothing shipped ON without Fable`s review.
BRIEF: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/s494p/prompt.md (label s494p, perf round 35, IDs 2110-2129, gen v2-1820).

=== THE GENERAL-PATH CENSUS (s494p, Opus, 2026-09-25) ===
QUESTION: can `.=` on the GENERAL path (a hash element, a package variable, `$self->{buf} .= $chunk`, an unlicensed lexical) append IN PLACE?  Only under an OWNERSHIP invariant: "an adjustable buffer is referenced by exactly one slot; whatever can RETAIN a value stores a simple-string SNAPSHOT".  perl's cost model allows it (perl copies on assignment, so a snapshot at the store keeps perl's complexity class).  The runtime's law today is the opposite (the SHARED-STRINGS note above *p-small-fixnum-strings*: strings are shared values, nothing writes into a string it did not make), and `to-string` returns a string argument ITSELF — so every value copy shares the object.

THE INVARIANT IS ALREADY BROKEN TODAY — by the one producer of adjustable strings in user boxes: an in-memory filehandle.  `open $fh, '>', \$buf; print $fh "a"; my $copy = $buf; $h{$buf} = 1; print $fh "b"` makes $copy, an array element, a hash value AND a hash KEY read "ab" (perl: "a"; the key mutates inside the `equal` table, `exists $h{"a"}` goes false).  FILED #2111 (scratch/s494p/memfh.pl).  So the chokepoints below are owed for correctness whether or not the general append ships.

RETAINING SITES in cl/ (counted on s494p's tree; the grep patterns are in the s494p session log section):
| class | sites | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| scalar store `box-set` (75 callers funnel into it; 2 store arms: the plain fast path and the general `v` path) | 1 fn, 2 arms | WOULD NEED A SNAPSHOT TEST — cost measured below |
| direct `(setf (p-box-value …))` | 30 (2 of them ARE box-set's arms) | READ one by one: 6 are the in-memory FH PRODUCER (%p-open-memory's 5 modes + %psos-buf), 5 tie untie/STORE writes and 2 `local` save/restore put back the slot's OWN earlier value (owner, safe), 7 chomp/chop/s///-result writes store FRESH strings (subseq / regex replace), 4 defelem magic, 2 autoviv reference stores, 1 dirhandle, 1 p-scalar-= reference arm -> NONE of the 28 needs a test once the producer is fixed |
| raw element store `%p-storable-raw` (13 references: push/unshift/splice/list-assign/literal/hash store) | 1 fn | WOULD NEED A SNAPSHOT TEST (it parks `inner` raw) |
| element COPY arms `(make-p-box inner)` (%p-array-store-scalar fast path under PCL_RAW_ELEMS=0, %p-map-copy-scalar, flatten patch pass, …) | ~151 of 241 `make-p-box` calls take a non-literal value | CANNOT BE GUARDED site by site; only by testing inside the constructor (every box allocation pays) |
| hash KEYS | `%p-gethash-store` 7 callers + 25 `(setf (gethash (to-string …` / `key` sites | WOULD NEED A SNAPSHOT TEST — first ONE hash-key coercion helper (there is none: each site calls to-string) |
| raw `vector-push-extend` of values into arrays / list temporaries | 119 | CANNOT BE GUARDED exhaustively (most push fresh or internal values; each would need reading) |
| closures, `@_`, foreach, `\$x`, `local` | — | COPIES NOTHING — they alias the BOX, not the value: the owner stays the one slot |
| deferred match captures ($& $` $' @- …) | 1 | COPIES ALREADY — do-regex-match coerces a non-simple subject to a simple-string once per call (tasks #680/#477: "it also pins *match-subject* to a copy no str-buffer append can mutate") |
| pos() tables (*p-match-pos*) | 12 refs | NOT A RETAINER — keyed by the BOX (eq) |
| sort decoration / caches (%p-sort-*) | 46 refs | TRANSIENT — values live for one sort; only a comparator that appends to its own operand could observe it |
| XS bridge (cl/pcl-xs.lisp) | 6 to-string | COPIES ALREADY — sb-ext:string-to-octets |
| TAP layer (cl/pcl-test.lisp) | — | TRANSIENT (compares and prints) |
| symbol names (`intern`, symbolic refs) | 72 intern refs | COPIES ALREADY (SBCL copies a non-simple name into a new symbol) |
| bless class name, die/warn payload in a condition object, %ENV (setenv copies) | 1 + ~3 | bless and the die payload WOULD NEED A TEST; %ENV copies |

THE COST OF THE TEST (measured): variant runtime scratch/s494p/variant/snap-runtime.lisp = box-set's two store arms + %p-storable-raw's raw-string arm test `(and (stringp v) (not (simple-string-p v)))` and coerce; BENCH_K=5, interleaved A/B on the control set (log scratch/s494p/m4-boxset-snapshot-ab.log, B/A = variant/ship - 1):
    arrhash +1.3  arrhash-k -1.9  fib(27)x -1.6  gcdrec -1.6  fibret +1.0  subret -1.9  methret +0.7  strcat +0.6
    sortnum +1.4  feread -2.2  feread2 +1.3  feread3 +2.5  feargs +1.1  ovlsub -6.9  moo-objs +2.9  textproc -0.8
    mapmulti -0.9  mapsingle -0.3     (load 1.8-2.5)
  The A-vs-A CONTROL PAIR in the same window (scratch/s494p/m4-control-pair.log, B = a byte-identical copy of A) spans -6.1 % (sortnum) to +3.0 %, so no row moved outside the noise band.  The per-call cost, isolated (scratch/s494p/snapmicro.lisp -> m4-snapshot-micro.log, 50 M calls of box-set's fast path with and without the test): +0.40-0.46 ns per STRING store (~8 % of that fast path alone), ~0.5 ns per number store.  FLAG: NOT resolvable at the control set's noise (the 1 % bar cannot be decided by it); the micro number is the honest one — ~0.4 ns per store, ~8 % of box-set's fast path in isolation.

RECOMMENDATION:
1. Fix #2111 FIRST, with the chokepoints that cost nothing measurable: the two box-set arms, %p-storable-raw, ONE new hash-key helper routed through the ~32 key sites, bless's class name.  That makes the in-memory-FH producer safe and is the prerequisite of everything below.
2. Do NOT ship a general in-place `.=` on top of that yet: the ~151 value-taking `make-p-box` calls and 119 raw `vector-push-extend` sites cannot be closed by reading them; the only closed form is a test in the p-box CONSTRUCTOR (every box allocation pays it, measure before proposing) PLUS an audit mode (PCL_STRBUF_AUDIT: assert at each retaining store that no non-simple string arrives) run over the gate + sweep + everyday to find the stragglers.  Until that audit is green the general append is a SILENT-WRONG generator (the #2111 shape, program-wide).
3. Meanwhile the COMPILE-TIME route keeps paying: s494p's member 3 licensed the modifier and `$s = $s . X` spellings; #2114 (a literal-RHS list declaration) is the next one.  `$self->{buf} .= $chunk` is the shape neither route reaches — it needs step 2.
Candidate built behind a switch: NOT built beyond the measurement variant (the census says the switch could not be turned on safely; an OFF-switch A/B on the shapes table would measure an unshippable lever).

=== DONE (s494p, Opus, 2026-09-26; resumed after a reboot by a fresh agent in s498) ===
MEMBER 1 (measure) DONE.  scaling.pl BEFORE flagged exactly the three rows perl does not: `str .= loop` x29.3, `unshift loop` x15.2, `shift drain` x16.4 (m1-scaling-before.pcl.log; the recursion row crashes rc=1 = #2113).  S1 decline reasons, by name (PCL_B_DEBUG): the statement-MODIFIER spelling reached the annotator through the v1 per-statement fallback (native_root 0, reason `write-compound`) -- a ROUTE accident, not a safety condition; the `while` shape was declined by its `my ($s,$i) = ("",0)` LIST declaration (a write-list, filed #2114); `$s = $s . X` was not in write_ops as a `.=`.  `shift` on `@_`: raw-params subs (fib/fibret/subret/methret) bind without p-shift; `(p-shift @_)` only in general subs (`my $self = shift; my %o = @_`).
MEMBER 2 (the WINDOW) SHIPPED, runtime-only: ONE helper advances / retreats the array header's window via sb-kernel:set-array-header (displaced-p T, the vacated slot cleared); shift, splice(@a,0,K) with no replacement list, unshift into front room; reset on drain-to-empty; unshift with no front room reallocates once with geometric front slack.  SHORT arrays (<= 16, not already displaced) keep copying: threshold A/B m2-shortshift-ab.log ship 1.221 s vs old 1.378 (12.8 % faster) vs always-window 1.473 (6.5 % slower).  Steady queue: slide-in-place vs let-growth-reallocate measured (m2-slide-vs-grow.log), GROW kept (slide never cheaper).  Load-time self-test on a scratch array; on any wrong answer the copying arm is used and stderr says once `PCL: array window unavailable on this SBCL (<version>); shift and unshift are O(n)`.  PLATFORM-TOUCHING (SBCL-internal header call; pure Lisp, no OS call) -- for Fable's install-matrix run.  Guard Pl/t/array-window-01.t (33 rows; 13 fail on the base).

REST` is the append via ONE predicate Pl::VarAnnotator::append_rest.  No S1 condition weakened.  corpus-diff 38/111 by class (layout / foreach-range / topic `$_` capture removed / p-my-= -> p-scalar-= / raw slot / %p-push1), compile +2.0 %.  Guard Pl/t/loop-modifier-01.t.  ir-spec Â§2.2 / Â§2.3 / Â§6.2.
MEMBER 4 (general path) CENSUS ONLY, nothing shipped: see the census section above; its step 2 is filed as #2115.  What kills shipping it now: ~151 value-taking make-p-box sites + 119 raw vector-push-extend sites cannot be closed by reading, and the invariant is already broken by the in-memory FH (#2111).
